label: rem:binding-scale-catalan-argument
title: Argument for the Borromean–Catalan binding scale (not a proof)
html:
Argument (not a proof). The Borromean complement decomposes into two regular ideal octahedra, each of volume 4G (where G = \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) is the Clausen function evaluated at \pi/2). The equality \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G is a theorem of hyperbolic geometry, not a numerical approximation. The volume is known to arbitrary precision as a mathematical constant.

The scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G connects:

  • Lepton sector (m_e): the electron mass sets the overall energy scale. This is the single measurement input.
  • Baryon topology (8G): the Borromean link invariant \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) encodes the three-quark confinement geometry.

The same scale \alpha appears at two levels:

  1. Nuclear binding: \mathfrak{m}(Z, N) = M_{\mathrm{free}} + \alpha \cdot \Phi_{\mathrm{atom}}, where \Phi < 0 for bound nuclei.
  2. Quark confinement: \Delta m = \alpha \cdot |\Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{quark}}|, giving the neutron--proton mass splitting.

What this argument does not supply is a derivation that the binding correction of the atomic mass formula is scaled by \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) rather than by some other invariant of the Borromean closure. That identification is the conjectural step.

Comparison boundary. Evaluated with the CODATA electron mass, the uncertainty of \alpha is the measurement uncertainty of m_e (\pm 3 \times 10^{-8} relative); the factor 8G carries none.
